# EhOsContract.Domain

The Spark extension behind `use EhOsContract.Domain`.

One top-level section, so every entity is written straight into the module body:
subdomains, contexts with their glossary, actors, subjects of personal data, value types,
entities, external systems and the relations between contexts. The vocabulary is closed:
a domain module cannot add extensions.

The structs this module defines are what Spark builds from each declaration. They are the
extension's own data and stay inside it: readers get plain data from
`EhOsContract.Model`, never these structs.

## domain

The vocabulary contracts share.



| Entity | What it declares |
|--------|------------------|
| [`subdomain`](domain-subdomain.md) | A part of the business the domain covers, named, with its kind. |
| [`context`](domain-context.md) | A bounded context: a part of the domain with its own language. |
| [`actor`](domain-actor.md) | Who issues commands: a kind of person, or a system. |
| [`subject`](domain-subject.md) | A kind of person whose personal data may be erased. |
| [`value`](domain-value.md) | A value type: one built-in type with an optional unit, or a set of fields. |
| [`entity`](domain-entity.md) | A thing with an identity whose lifecycle the application's code or another system keeps, outside this log: a period, an item of a catalogue. |
| [`external`](domain-external.md) | An external system, named after what it does for the business, not after the vendor. |
| [`relation`](domain-relation.md) | How two contexts relate: one of the eight context-mapping patterns. |
